answer: A farm generating text without memory of its own history as a result fails the binding, and thus it has to store and read state per alias. Bindings are kept in prism, verified in willow, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 6 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the falcon check. That bill is paid per identity, so 248 aliases cost 94 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
